data.narrative:
Quaise Energy is a Series A climate and energy company founded by Carlos Araque and Matthew Houde that has raised $134M to date. The broader Climate & Energy sector includes nine peer companies—one public (Lnza) and eight private firms including Helion, Redwood Materials, QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, and Electric Hydrogen—though none provide sufficiently comparable valuation benchmarks at the same stage and tier.

Given the absence of a robust peer-median dataset, valuation relies on stage-progression methodology. Using total capital raised ($134M) as a proxy for post-money value, a typical Series A to subsequent-stage step-up multiplier of 2.0x yields an implied valuation of $268M. This single-method triangulation is inherently narrow; applying standard sensitivity bounds of ±15% around the point estimate generates a range of $228M (low) to $308M (high).

The $268M median reflects current market evidence but carries material uncertainty. Key risks include the scarcity of directly comparable private financings in deep-tech energy, stage-progression assumptions that may not hold for frontier-technology timelines, and the absence of revenue or pathway-to-profitability data. Any refined valuation would benefit from additional comparable transactions or disclosure of unit economics and technical milestones. The range should be treated as illustrative rather than definitive.
